P1 Next-Action Prediction Results

Overview

We predict whether P1 cooperates in round \(t\) of a supergame using several model families. The baseline models use game metadata (\(g\), \(l\), \(\delta\)) plus P1’s own past-action n-grams (last 1–5 actions, one-hot encoded). These are fit with OLS, Lasso, and SVR (RBF kernel approximation + LinearSVR).

IRL-SG is the 6-parameter learning model of Fudenberg & Karreskog Rehbinder (2024, Appendix D): a logistic initial-round reinforcement learner with semi-grim memory-1 transitions at non-initial rounds. We report two variants: IRL-SG (defaults) uses the paper’s published parameters \((\alpha, \beta, \lambda, p_{CC}, p_{CD/DC}, p_{DD})\), while IRL-SG (MLE) re-estimates those parameters via maximum likelihood on the training set—as the paper does in its one-step-ahead prediction exercise.

Train/test split is at the sequence level (80/20 of supergame rows) for the baseline models and at the session level (80/20 of sessions) for IRL-SG. Both are stratified on unique \((g, l, \delta)\) treatments.

Sample sizes

Longer n-gram requirements exclude shorter sequences.
